_comment_top: spaarke-ai-architecture-redesign-r1 task 008 (FR-P0-07 read half) — seed row for the dataverse.read_query read tool. GA-MCP-contract-frozen per ADR-039: sprk_toolid local segment equals the GA Dataverse MCP tool name 'read_query'; the single required argument is 'querytext' exactly as GA (research note notes/audit-inputs/research-dataverse-mcp-2026-07.md; Learn ms.date 2026-06-05).
_comment_routing: Runtime invocation routes to DataverseReadQueryHandler via sprk_handlerclass. Auto-discovered (ADR-010). P2 loop projects the LLM-facing function name from sprk_toolid.
_comment_obo: spec MUST rule (task-012 audit): the query executes through IDataverseUserClient under the calling user's OBO token — the user's security roles + row-level security filter every row. NO app-only path.
_comment_side_effect: sprk_sideeffectclass = 100000000 (Read). Read-only is enforced mechanically: DataverseSqlQueryTranslator only parses SELECT; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/DDL are rejected with a redirect to the dataverse write tools.
_comment_dialect: Native transport translates the GA read_query SQL dialect to OData. Single-table core supported (SELECT [TOP n] explicit-columns FROM table [WHERE column-to-literal predicates with AND/OR/parens, LIKE, IS NULL] [ORDER BY]). GA-unsupported features (subqueries, HAVING, DISTINCT, UNION, OFFSET, CAST/CONVERT, WITH) rejected with GA-matching messages. TDS-only GA features (JOIN, GROUP BY, aggregates, GETDATE) rejected with clear reformulation guidance — swap to MCP transport later lifts these without a contract change.
_comment_grounding: ADR-039 grounding: the table's primary id column is auto-added to the selection; every row carries '@citation.path' = tables/{t}/records/{id} and adapter-level citation metadata.
_comment_consumption: Read by scripts/Seed-TypedHandlers.ps1. Idempotent — UPSERT by sprk_handlerclass + sprk_toolcode with sprk_name 'SYS-%' filter.
sprk_description: Executes a read-only SQL SELECT against Dataverse under the calling user's permissions and returns rows with record-id citations. Use dataverse.describe FIRST to get the table's column logical names and types, then construct a query that strictly follows the supported dialect: SELECT [TOP n] explicit column list FROM one table [WHERE simple column-to-literal predicates combined with AND/OR] [ORDER BY column ASC|DESC]. NOT supported: SELECT *, JOIN, GROUP BY, aggregates (COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX), subqueries, DISTINCT, HAVING, UNION, OFFSET, GETDATE(). For distributions/aggregations (counts by category), SELECT the category column across rows (TOP up to 200) and aggregate the values YOURSELF from the result. LOOKUP columns (e.g. sprk_practicearea on sprk_matter) ARE selectable and return the referenced record's GUID — query the referenced table (e.g. sprk_practicearea_ref) to map GUIDs to display names. Choice columns return numeric option values — map them to labels via dataverse.describe. Default row cap 50 (TOP max 200). Results respect the current user's Dataverse security roles and row-level security. Spaarke entity map (use these logical names): 'matter'/'case'/'deal' = sprk_matter (key columns sprk_mattername, sprk_matternumber, sprk_matterdescription, statuscode; lookups sprk_practicearea to sprk_practicearea_ref, sprk_mattertype to sprk_mattertype_ref, sprk_assignedattorney1 to contact, sprk_externalaccount to account). 'project'/'workstream' = sprk_project (sprk_projectname, sprk_projectnumber). 'document'/'contract'/'file' = sprk_document (sprk_documentname, sprk_filename, sprk_documenttype, sprk_filesummary; lookups sprk_matter, sprk_project). People = contact; client companies = account; law firms/vendors = sprk_organization.
